sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: LARGE SCALE MID-UPPER LEVEL TROUGH...CURRENTLY MOVING SWD THROUGH WRN CANADA PER WATER VAPOR IMAGERY...WILL PROGRESS SWD INTO THE NWRN STATES TODAY WHILE A PORTION OF THIS TROUGH ALSO MOVES EWD INTO CENTRAL CANADA/NRN PLAINS. MEANWHILE...THE EVOLUTION OF THIS LARGE SCALE TROUGH WILL SUPPORT A PAIR OF PHASED SHORTWAVE TROUGHS ADVANCING ENEWD ACROSS THE DAKOTAS/NEB TO MN AND THE MID MO VALLEY BY LATE AFTERNOON. THESE LATTER FEATURES SHOULD DE-AMPLIFY AS THEY TRACK NEWD INTO THE UPPER GREAT LAKES TOWARD A BUILDING RIDGE FROM THE UPPER OH VALLEY INTO QUEBEC. IN THE LOW LEVELS...A COLD FRONT TRAILING SSWWD FROM THE ERN DAKOTAS TO THE CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS WILL ADVANCE EWD THROUGH THE UPPER MS VALLEY...WHILE THE WRN EXTENSION MOVES SSEWD THROUGH THE CENTRAL PLAINS. BY 12Z SATURDAY...THE COLD FRONT SHOULD EXTEND FROM THE UPPER GREAT LAKES SWWD THROUGH ERN IA TO SERN KS...AND THEN WWD INTO THE NRN TX/OK PANHANDLES REGION. MEANWHILE...A SECONDARY COLD FRONT IS EXPECTED TO SPREAD ESEWD ACROSS THE NRN PLAINS. A WARM FRONT EXTENDING SEWD FROM IA TO THE LOWER OH VALLEY IS NOT EXPECTED TO MOVE MUCH TODAY...BUT WILL PROVIDE A TRIPLE POINT OVER CENTRAL IA WHERE THE COLD FRONT INTERSECTS THIS BOUNDAR

sections.title: ERN SD/NEB TO UPPER MS VALLEY AND UPPER GREAT LAKES
sections.text: AT 12Z...CLUSTERS OF TSTMS /SOME POSSIBLY SEVERE/ ARE EXPECTED TO BE ONGOING ACROSS MUCH OF MN SSWWD THROUGH IA TO ERN NEB WITHIN WAA REGIME ALONG CORRIDOR OF SSWLY LLJ WHICH SHOULD BE EXTENDING FROM THE CENTRAL PLAINS TO ERN MN/WRN WI. GIVEN THE EXTENSIVE COVERAGE OF TSTMS/CONVECTIVE CLOUDINESS AT THE START OF THE DAY 1 PERIOD...SURFACE HEATING MAY BE LIMITED TO ERN PERIPHERY OF THE MORNING TSTM CLUSTERS AND IN THE WAKE OF THESE STORMS ALONG THE COLD FRONT. DESPITE SOMEWHAT LIMITED SURFACE HEATING...STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES EXTENDING EWD INTO THE UPPER MS TO LOWER MO VALLEYS COMBINED WITH A VERY MOIST RESIDUAL AIR MASS WILL SUPPORT MODERATE INSTABILITY ACROSS THE SLIGHT RISK AREA...WITH VERY STRONG INSTABILITY /MLCAPE EXCEEDING 2500 J PER KG/ ACROSS MUCH OF IA. 40-50 KT BAND OF WSWLY MIDLEVEL WINDS WILL EXTEND FROM THE NRN HIGH PLAINS TO UPPER MS VALLEY/UPPER GREAT LAKES REGION. THIS WILL RESULT IN EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR AROUND 40 KT ALONG AND E OF THE LEADING COLD FRONT TO SUPPORT ORGANIZED STORMS/SUPERCELLS WITH NEW TSTMS THAT DEVELOPMENT BOTH E AND W OF THE ONGOING MORNING TSTM CLUSTERS. GIVEN AVAILABLE INSTABILITY/SHEAR VALUES...THIS ACTIVITY WILL PRODUCE BOTH HAIL AND DAMAGIN

sections.title: ERN ND/NWRN MN
sections.text: AIR MASS DESTABILIZATION IN THE WAKE OF ANY MORNING ACTIVITY IS EXPECTED TO SUPPORT MODERATE INSTABILITY IN ADVANCE OF THE SECONDARY COLD FRONT. FORCING FOR ASCENT ALONG THIS BOUNDARY AND WITH A SHORTWAVE TROUGH SPREADING EWD INTO THIS REGION BY AFTERNOON WILL SUPPORT TSTMS. EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR 30-35 KT WILL SUPPORT BOTH MULTICELLS AND SUPERCELLS...WITH HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS THE PRIMARY THREATS INTO THE EARLY EVENING. THIS ACTIVITY SHOULD THEN WEAKEN AS IT MOVES INTO NORTH CENTRAL MN WHERE THE AIR MASS WILL LIKELY BE MORE STABLE/RAIN COOLED.

sections.title: KS/NRN MO
sections.text: MOIST AIR MASS ACROSS ERN KS INTO MO BENEATH ERN EXTENT OF STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES WILL BECOME MODERATELY UNSTABLE AS STRONG SURFACE HEATING OCCURS IN ADVANCE OF THE SSEWD MOVING COLD FRONT. TSTMS SHOULD DEVELOP ALONG THIS BOUNDARY BY PEAK HEATING WITH EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR 30-35 KT SUPPORTING BOTH MULTICELLS AND SUPERCELLS PRODUCING STRONG/DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL. THIS ACTIVITY SHOULD BE PRIMARILY DIURNALLY DRIVEN...THOUGH SOME ACTIVITY MAY LINGER AFTER DARK ACROSS NRN MO. ..PETERS/BOTHWELL.. 08/13/2010

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: WRN NEB/SD SHORTWAVE TROUGH EXPECTED TO MOVE ENE INTO MN BY THIS EVE AND TO N OF LK SUPERIOR EARLY SAT AS STRONGER UPSTREAM DISTURBANCE NOW ENTERING WRN MT CONTINUES SE INTO WY. ELSEWHERE... CLOSED HIGH SHOULD REMAIN STNRY OFF THE BC CST WHILE RIDGE PERSISTS FROM THE SRN PLNS TO THE OH VLY. AT THE SFC...PATTERN WILL BE COMPLICATED BY LARGE AREAS OF CONVECTIVE OUTFLOW FROM OVERNIGHT MCSS. OUTFLOW BOUNDARY NOW EXTENDING EWD FROM ERN SD SFC LOW SHOULD BE ONE FOCUS FOR STORM DEVELOPMENT TODAY...WITH LEAD COLD FRONT ATTENDANT TO NEB/SD UPR TROUGH PROVIDING ANOTHER. THE FRONT WILL MOVE E ACROSS THE UPR MS VLY...AND SSE ACROSS THE CNTRL PLNS. MEANWHILE...A SECOND COLD FRONT...NOW OVER ND/MT... SHOULD MOVE ESE ACROSS THE NRN PLNS THROUGH TONIGHT. AT THE SAME TIME...DIFFUSE WARM FRONT NOW OVER ERN IA/IL EXPECTED TO MAKE ONLY MINIMAL PROGRESS NEWD INTO THE LWR OH VLY.

sections.title: ERN NEB/ERN SD TO MID/UPR MS VLY AND UPR GRT LKS
sections.text: STRONG TO SVR TSTMS EXPECTED TO PERSIST THROUGH LATER THIS MORNING OVER CNTRL/SRN MN E/SE INTO WI IN ZONE OF PERSISTENT LOW-LVL WAA/RICH MOISTURE TRANSPORT WHERE SSWLY LLJ ENCOUNTERS DIFFUSE WARM FRONT AND AFOREMENTIONED W/E OUTFLOW BOUNDARY. MANY OF THE STORMS WILL BE SLIGHTLY ELEVATED. BUT COMBINATION OF DEEP EML AND HIGH PW /AROUND 2 INCHES/ COULD CONTINUE TO YIELD DMGG SFC WINDS...SOME HAIL...AND POSSIBLY A TORNADO OR TWO IN ASSOCIATION WITH ANY EMBEDDED MESOVORTICES. LATER TODAY...SFC HEATING AND ASCENT WITH NEB/SD UPR TROUGH SHOULD SUPPORT AN ADDITIONAL ROUND OF SVR STORMS ALONG LEAD COLD FRONT FROM WRN/SRN MN SW INTO ERN NEB AND WRN/NRN IA...WHERE STEEP MID-LVL LAPSE RATES AND HIGH PW SHOULD SUPPORT MODERATE TO STRONG DESTABILIZATION WITH SBCAPE TO 3500 J/KG. 35-40 KT WSWLY MID-LVL FLOW ASSOCIATED WITH EJECTING TROUGH WILL PROVIDE SUFFICIENT SHEAR FOR SUSTAINED STORMS/SUPERCELLS WITH LARGE HAIL AND DMGG WINDS. THE STRONGEST LOW-LVL SHEAR /0-1 KM SRH OF 100-200 M2 PER S2/ SHOULD EXIST ALONG ERN SIDE OF 30-40 KT SSWLY LLJ EXTENDING FROM IA TOWARD UPR GRT LKS...WHERE THE GREATEST TORNADO THREAT SHOULD EXIST. ONE OR MORE MCSS MAY EVOLVE FROM THE AFTN STORMS. THESE SHOULD BOTH MO

sections.title: ERN ND INTO NRN MN
sections.text: LOW-LVL DESTABILIZATION ALONG SECOND COLD FRONT AND BENEATH NRN PART OF EJECTING UPR TROUGH MAY YIELD AN ENVIRONMENT FAVORABLE FOR AFTN TSTMS. MODERATE INSTABILITY/RELATIVELY COOL AIR ALOFT COUPLED WITH 35-40 KT DEEP SWLY SHEAR MAY SUPPORT A FEW CLUSTERS/BANDS OF MULTICELLS AND SUPERCELLS WITH HAIL AND DMGG WIND THROUGH EARLY EVE. THIS ACTIVITY SHOULD WEAKEN AFTER SUNSET.

sections.title: KS/NRN MO
sections.text: MOIST AIR OVER ERN KS INTO MO BENEATH SE EXTENT OF EML PLUME WILL BECOME MODERATELY UNSTABLE AS STRONG SURFACE HEATING OCCURS AHEAD OF COLD FRONT AND ALONG LEE TROUGH SE OF FRONT. TSTMS SHOULD FORM ALONG THIS BOUNDARY BY PEAK HEATING...WITH INSTABILITY AND 25-30 KT DEEP WLY SHEAR ON SRN FRINGE OF NEB/IA WSWLY JET SUPPORTING BOTH MULTICELLS AND A FEW SUPERCELLS WITH DMGG WIND AND SVR HAIL. THE STRONGEST STORMS SHOULD BE MAINLY DIURNAL... ALTHOUGH NOCTURNAL STRENGTHENING OF LLJ MAY ALLOW A S OR SE-MOVING MCS OR TWO TO LINGER AFTER DARK OVER KS/MO. ..CORFIDI/HURLBUT.. 08/13/2010

sections.title: UPPER MS TO MIDDLE MO RIVER VALLEYS
sections.text: COMPLEX SYSTEM EVOLUTION ONLY BECOMING A LITTLE MORE RESOLVABLE AS OF LATE AFTERNOON. MODEST LARGE SCALE ASCENT ASSOCIATED WITH LEADING SHORT WAVE TROUGH EJECTING NEWD ACROSS THE NCNTRL U.S. WILL CONTINUE TO PROMOTE TSTM DEVELOPMENT WITHIN VERY MOIST AND WARMING AIRMASS. SEVERAL MESOSCALE COLD POOLS AND OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES AMONGST THE SYNOPTIC FEATURES INCLUDING SFC LOW/WARM FRONT AND ADVANCING COLD FRONT AND PRE-FRONTAL/THERMAL TROUGH COMPLICATE THE OVERALL STORM EVOLUTION INTO THE EVENING. IT IS BEGINNING TO APPEAR THAT TWO AREAS WILL EXPERIENCE SLIGHTLY GREATER SEVERE WEATHER POTENTIAL. THE FIRST AREA WILL BE THE REGION OF SERN WI SWWD ACROSS NRN IL/SERN IA AND INTO NRN MO AND PERHAPS NERN KS. STORMS ALONG CONVECTIVE OUTFLOWS AND AHEAD OF THE FAVORABLE LARGE SCALE FORCING WILL CONTINUE TO MOVE INTO LOCALLY STRONG INSTABILITY ON THE SRN FRINGE OF STRONGER FLOW ALOFT. PRIMARY THREAT FROM THIS CONVECTION WILL CONTINUE TO BE DAMAGING WIND GUSTS GIVEN HOT BOUNDARY LAYER AND DCAPE VALUES IN EXCESS OF 1000 J/KG. IT APPEARS POSSIBLE THAT ONE OR TWO LINEAR MCSS MAY EVOLVE FROM THIS ACTIVITY AND SPREAD SOUTH AND EAST WITH WIND DAMAGE POTENTIAL INTO THIS EVENING. GIVEN HIGH MOISTURE CONTENT
